messages.author: 07e8757db07db23b
messages.subject: MathematicaStan
parts:
I just have posted a beta release of a Mathematica package to interact with CmdStan

https://github.com/vincent-picaud/MathematicaStan/

This is a first release, only tested under Linux, however I think it can be useful for Mathematica + Stan users.

Any feedback is welcome.

Vincent Picaud

ps: you can view a pdf copy of the Mathematica notebook associated to the Bernoulli example.

messages.author: 07e8757db07db23b
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] MathematicaStan
parts:
Again thank you for your welcome message.

As a complement to my Andrew answer, I have chosen the  A-GPL3 licence which is AFAIK also the licence of the other packages JuliaStan, RStan...

I would be happy to share and maintain this package, we "only" have to get some feedbacks to be sure that it is useful and it respects the quality Stan deserves.

If you want, you can mention it and host it on the stan-dev repo. Just proceed the way which is the more convenient for you. I do agree with the idea.

Vincent

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] MathematicaStan
parts:
Our other interfaces are using standard GPL, not the Affero version (AGPL),
which is even more restrictively copyleft:

https://www.gnu.org/licenses/why-affero-gpl.html

There's also the issue of what's compatible with Mathematica---I have
no idea what the standard is there for licensing and what options
Mathematica provides for licensing versions as a back-end for products.

It's very confusing to me where the GPL boundaries are with respect
to what constitutes a derivative work.

- Bob

ooh, sorry about the "A"GPL, I have not noticed that when I filled up
the GitHub form.

As this is a purely personal project and my goal is to make this work available there is no problem on my side
I just changed the project licence to GPLv3.

Le mardi 13 septembre 2016 16:13:35 UTC+2, Bob Carpenter a écrit :
Our other interfaces are using standard GPL, not the Affero version (AGPL),
which is even more restrictively copyleft:

https://www.gnu.org/licenses/why-affero-gpl.html

There's also the issue of what's compatible with Mathematica---I have
no idea what the standard is there for licensing and what options
Mathematica provides for licensing versions as a back-end for products.

I do not know, but to my mind, I think the Mathematica package itself (which is only an ASCII file),
can be freely distributed. Obviously to use it you need Mathematica software with its licence.

It's very confusing to me where the GPL boundaries are with respect
to what constitutes a derivative work.

- Bob
